meta.title: Digital Exhibition — Headless Migration
meta.subtitle: Cloudflare front-end + slimmed WordPress backend
meta.client: TU/e — Built Environment, Digital Exhibition platform
meta.author: marco@tech-paw.com
meta.summary: Move Digital Exhibition to a headless architecture: a Nuxt 3 / Vue / Tailwind front-end, built as a fully static site on Cloudflare, that reads the existing WordPress REST API, while the WordPress install on the TU/e server is stripped back to a lean content API. Media moves to one Cloudflare R2 bucket shared by live, staging and the app, and transactional mail moves to Microsoft Graph via Azure or to Brevo (to be decided). Both the WordPress backend (wp-content) and the front-end are under Git version control. There is no automated pipeline: Git is connected to the server's control panel, so files are changed, checked on staging, and then merged into production by hand. The merge of staging into live is planned after 6 November.

workstreams.name: Cloudflare front-end (Nuxt)
workstreams.goal: A production Nuxt 3 front-end, served as a fully static site on Cloudflare, that renders the whole Digital Exhibition from the WordPress REST API, with no upstream host or CORS exposed to the browser.
workstreams.context: Lives in frontend/digital-exhibition, in its own Git repository. Every route — pages, archives, every entry and the home page — is pre-rendered at build time; the home hero is picked in the browser on each visit. Site identity, menus and archive layout are read from WordPress (GET /wp-json/cd/v1/site). A build fails if WordPress can't answer, so Cloudflare keeps the previous complete deployment live. Only a few endpoints run at request time: the PDF proxy, the contact form, search and the site settings.

tasks.notes: server/api/pdf.get.ts — never wrapped by the route cache.

tasks.notes: composables/useWordpress.ts — useHomeFeed, useArchiveEntries, useArchiveIntro, useResolvedContent (permalink-style resolver).

tasks.notes: composables/useDflip.ts — dFlip assets self-hosted under public/dflip/assets/, PDFs served through server/api/pdf.get.ts (proxied, Range-aware). Figure captions now show each PDF's own filename instead of a shared prefix.

tasks.notes: 11 components under components/. Matches the live left-sidebar layout, drawer under lg.

tasks.title: Cross-year siblings timeline
tasks.notes: utils/siblings.ts — ports cd_inject_timeline_elementor(): slug base minus -YYYY + shared unit/category term.

tasks.title: Cloudflare deploy (static assets) + build trigger
tasks.notes: Pre-rendered pages are served as static assets (wrangler.jsonc); the Worker only runs for /api/*. Rebuilds start from WordPress with the Deploy Frontend button (Cloudflare deploy hook). Prerender concurrency is 1, with retries and a warm-up request, because the upstream host drops HTTP/2 streams under parallel load.

tasks.title: Runtime config & env for prod (WP_API_BASE, WP_SITE_URL)
tasks.notes: WP_API_BASE, WP_SITE_URL and the NUXT_PUBLIC_* values are environment variables; no domain is hardcoded. Point them at staging until the merge, then at live.

tasks.title: Error states, 404, slow-upstream resilience pass
tasks.notes: Verified — error.vue renders a generic statusCode/statusMessage page; [...slug].vue throws a real 404 for unresolved permalinks; EntryView falls back to excerpt + link-out when content.rendered is empty; server/api/wp/[...path].ts retries (3x) with a 30s timeout against the upstream; nitro prerender failOnError:false confirmed.

tasks.title: Cross-browser + mobile QA against the live site
tasks.notes: Cross-browser and mobile QA completed.

tasks.title: Static, settings-driven build
tasks.notes: Site identity, menus and archive definitions come from WordPress (cd/v1/site) and are used to discover and pre-render every route. Builds fail when required data is missing (PRERENDER_REQUIRE_WP). Logos and icon load from WordPress with bundled fallbacks; legacy URLs redirect; R2 upload paths are normalised in the rendered HTML.

tasks.title: Search page + route-fetch resilience
tasks.notes: The search page is pre-rendered and its results render in the browser. WordPress route fetching retries in smaller paginated requests, with clearer errors and longer timeouts for cold starts.

workstreams.name: Slim the TU/e WordPress server
workstreams.goal: Reduce the WordPress install on the TU/e server to what a content API actually needs — no front-end theme rendering weight, no dead code.
workstreams.context: backend/ holds a full WP core + wp-content. The front-end no longer needs WP to render pages for humans, only JSON (plus the Elementor single-region fallback).

tasks.title: Inventory the server: disk, plugins, themes, uploads size
tasks.notes: du -sh wp-content/*, list active vs inactive plugins, DB size, PHP version.

tasks.title: Identify 'useless folder' — the redundant LAMP-stack backend dir
tasks.notes: User flagged a leftover folder used for a local LAMP backend of WP. Confirm it is not referenced by wp-config.php / .htaccess, back it up, remove it.

tasks.title: Remove unused themes, keep one — and rename it
tasks.notes: Done — chique, chique-pro and twentytwentyfive removed; only the active theme is kept. On live the theme was renamed (tue-digital-exhibition) so it is no longer connected to the WordPress theme repository and automatic updates can't replace it. Staging keeps the old name until the merge.

tasks.title: Deactivate + delete confirmed-unused plugins
tasks.notes: Unused plugins removed. No longer installed: wordpress-importer, show-current-template, disable-wp-rest-api. WPForms Lite was deleted. better-search-replace stays until the staging→live merge; post-type-switcher stays while content is still being re-typed.

tasks.title: Document the final server layout in backend/README
tasks.notes: Done — backend/README explains what Git tracks and what it doesn't, and how to reinstall the third-party plugins (bin/install-plugins.sh). It holds no secrets: credentials live only in wp-config.php, which is not tracked; the repository carries a placeholder (wp-config.reference.php).

tasks.title: Deploy Frontend: confirmation + live build progress
tasks.notes: The admin-bar button asks for confirmation, then follows the Cloudflare build until it is live. The sticky Preview Changes button was removed and the admin sidebar now lists the day-to-day items first.

tasks.title: Site configuration REST endpoint (cd/v1/site)
tasks.notes: Exposes site identity, menus, footer details and archive configuration to the headless front-end. Part of the custom_dashboard plugin.

tasks.title: Media library: video support
tasks.notes: An ACF video file field plus a safe backfill script; selected uploads play in a native video player, and embeds still work.

tasks.title: PDF field + thumbnail regeneration with R2
tasks.notes: An ACF PDF file field, with legacy dFlip shortcodes backfilled into it. Thumbnails regenerate correctly alongside the media offloader (advmo-regenerate-thumbnails-compat).

workstreams.name: WordPress audit & plugin rationalisation
workstreams.goal: Decide, plugin by plugin, what stays, what is replaced, and what is removed — without touching the two heavy dependencies the content genuinely relies on.
workstreams.context: The plugins we use today are listed in the plugin audit below. Two heavy dependencies the content relies on and that we do not touch: ACF PRO and Elementor / Elementor Pro.

tasks.title: FileBird Pro → open replacement
tasks.notes: Replaced by Figuro Media, our own folder plugin. Folder assignments carried over: 438 folders and 3,943 files imported from FileBird.

tasks.title: DearFlip (dflip) → keep
tasks.notes: Decision: keep the plugin. The front-end self-hosts the dFlip assets (public/dflip) and streams PDFs through its own proxy (useDflip, server/api/pdf).

tasks.title: Keep — Advanced Custom Fields PRO (do not touch)
tasks.notes: Field data drives the REST payloads the front-end consumes. No change. Confirm ACF-to-REST exposure is on for the fields the front-end reads.

tasks.title: Keep — Elementor + Elementor Pro (do not touch)
tasks.notes: 2025–2026 batch of post/courses/seminars is authored in Elementor; content.rendered is empty for those and the front-end lifts elementor-location-single from the rendered page. Removing Elementor breaks that batch.

tasks.title: WP Toolkit — used live, important
tasks.notes: The live site uses WP Toolkit to manage the website and to apply updates and security fixes, so it matters. We need to understand what to do with it when staging is merged into live.

tasks.title: Comments — delete
tasks.notes: To do: delete comments site-wide (switch the setting off and close existing threads). No plugin needed.

tasks.title: Decide — WP Mail SMTP → Brevo or Microsoft Graph
tasks.notes: Waiting for TU/e to choose: Brevo (free plan, 300 emails a day) or Microsoft Graph via Azure. WP Mail SMTP then connects WordPress mail (password reset) to that service; the front-end contact form calls it directly (see 4.4).

tasks.title: Decide — custom_dashboard / show-current-template / post-type-switcher
tasks.notes: custom_dashboard is our own plugin and stays (Manage News, Quick Actions, Audit Content). post-type-switcher stays only while content is still being re-typed. show-current-template is no longer installed.

tasks.title: Ultimate Addons for Elementor (UAE) — keep
tasks.notes: The plugin folder is header-footer-elementor. Decision: keep it.

tasks.title: Decide — Yoast SEO (wordpress-seo)
tasks.notes: Confirmed yoast_head_json is in the REST output and consumed by the front-end. Yoast now only stores per-entry meta; all rendering is front-end. Title templates still worth tidying in Yoast (some double up the site name).

tasks.title: WPForms Lite — deleted
tasks.notes: Deleted. Forms are handled by the front-end contact form, not by this plugin.

tasks.title: WP Umbrella — waiting
tasks.notes: Waiting for TU/e: we don't know whether it is used by their theme, so it stays until they confirm. It also loads a must-use file (InitUmbrella.php).

workstreams.name: Assets, domain, staging & mail on Cloudflare
workstreams.goal: Media served from one shared Cloudflare R2 bucket, the domain set up for the app, a safe staging copy of the WordPress site, and transactional mail through Brevo or Microsoft Graph.

tasks.title: Move images & PDFs to R2
tasks.notes: Advanced Media Offloader sends uploads to one shared R2 bucket, used by live, staging and the app. The staging uploads folder was deleted, so staging reads only from R2. For now live keeps a duplicate of its uploaded images, and a backup of the live uploads folder is kept if needed.

tasks.title: Add the domain to Cloudflare — depends on the hosting decision
tasks.notes: Waiting on the hosting decision (Cloudflare or somewhere else; Jonathan suggests Bunny.net). Planned layout: digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl shows the app; live. and staging. subdomains hold the two WordPress sites. Needs TU/e DNS.

tasks.title: Stand up a staging environment of the current WP site
tasks.notes: Staging has two jobs: testing new functions on the WordPress site and, in an emergency, replicating live to test the site or find errors. The staging and production databases are not synchronised, but both are up to date.

tasks.title: Transactional mail from the front-end (Brevo or Microsoft Graph)
tasks.notes: The contact form is built (components/ContactForm.vue + server/api/contact.post.ts, with validation and honeypot). The handler only logs for now; the mail call is a marked TODO until TU/e chooses Brevo or Microsoft Graph via Azure.

tasks.title: R2 lifecycle / caching / cost check
tasks.notes: Cache-Control on R2 objects, Cloudflare cache rules, confirm egress stays in free tier, document the re-sync procedure for new uploads.

workstreams.name: SEO on the front-end
workstreams.goal: The Nuxt front-end owns all discoverability: per-page meta, Open Graph, structured data, sitemap, robots — sourced from Yoast fields via REST.
workstreams.context: The front-end is currently noindex everywhere (robots.txt Disallow: /, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag via public/_headers). That must be lifted deliberately at cutover.

tasks.title: Per-route meta from yoast_head_json
tasks.notes: Implemented — utils/seo.ts maps yoast_head_json → title/description/canonical/OG/Twitter; composables/useSeo.ts wires it via useHead. Verified against /privacy-policy/, /contact/, entries.

tasks.title: Structured data (JSON-LD)
tasks.notes: Implemented — Yoast's schema @graph is passed through with WP-origin URLs rewritten to the public host; home feed emits a hand-written WebSite + Organization graph.

tasks.title: Dynamic sitemap.xml
tasks.notes: Implemented — server/routes/sitemap.xml.ts enumerates pages + archives + all entries from the proxy (161 URLs). 404s while not indexable.

tasks.title: Canonical strategy: switch to the real domain
tasks.notes: utils/seo.rewriteOrigin() already rewrites every WordPress URL (canonical, og:url, schema) to NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL. At go-live set that to digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl.

tasks.title: Lift noindex at cutover
tasks.notes: Gated behind NUXT_PUBLIC_INDEXABLE (default false): while false every route emits noindex + no JSON-LD + sitemap 404. Flip together with public/robots.txt and public/_headers (checklist added to both files).

tasks.title: Social / link-preview cards (OG image on a served host)
tasks.notes: buildSeoHead now sends page URLs (canonical/og:url/JSON-LD) to the front-end host but keeps /wp-content media URLs on public.mediaUrl (the WP box now, R2 later) so og:image never 404s. og:image:secure_url/type/alt + twitter:image:alt added. public/robots.txt allow-lists facebookexternalhit / Twitterbot / LinkedInBot / Slackbot / WhatsApp / etc. so shared links render a card while search stays blocked by the noindex meta. Note: _headers is Pages-only — no effect on a *.workers.dev deploy.

tasks.title: Investigate analytics & tracking
tasks.notes: Check whether we have or need Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Google Tag Manager and a cookie script.

workstreams.name: Version control (backend + front-end)
workstreams.goal: Put the WordPress backend (wp-content) and the front-end under Git, and ship changes by checking them on staging and merging them into production by hand — there is no automated pipeline.
workstreams.context: Git is connected to the server's control panel, so files are merged manually; Git is the version history and the backup. The front-end has its own repository, and Cloudflare builds the app from it.

tasks.title: Initialise a Git repo for wp-content
tasks.notes: Done — git repo initialised in backend/. .gitignore excludes wp-config.php (secrets), *.log, WP upgrade-temp dirs, compressx logs. wp-config.reference.php + README.md added.

tasks.title: Decide what version control tracks
tasks.notes: Tracked: our own code only — the figuro-folder, custom_dashboard and cloudflare-deploy-trigger plugins, the active theme, mu-plugins and maintenance files. Third-party plugins are git-ignored and reinstalled with bin/install-plugins.sh. WordPress core, wp-config.php, logs and uploads (→ R2) are not tracked.

tasks.title: Host the repo on GitHub
tasks.notes: Done — pushed to github.com/orso081980/digitalexhibition-backend, branch main, initial commit 35c6d25 (~13.8k files). Switched from private to public visibility per request.

tasks.title: Staging → production by manual merge (no pipeline)
tasks.notes: No GitHub Actions: Git is connected to the server's control panel, so files are merged by hand, after they have been checked on staging. Planned after 6 November: the staging files and database are merged into live, unless more content is added in the meantime.

tasks.title: Version control for the front-end
tasks.notes: The Nuxt app has its own Git repository (private on GitHub). Cloudflare builds the app from it, and the Deploy Frontend button in WordPress starts a new build.

architecture.before: Browser → WordPress (Elementor theme renders HTML) on TU/e LAMP box. Media, mail, SEO all inside WP.
architecture.after: Browser → Cloudflare (Nuxt, pre-rendered static pages served as files; only /api/* runs as a Worker) → /api/wp proxy → WordPress REST API (content source only). Media → one shared Cloudflare R2 bucket. Mail → Brevo or Microsoft Graph via Azure, to be decided. SEO and layout owned by Nuxt. Backend and front-end are under Git; backend file changes are checked on staging and merged into production by hand.
